transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
A sell-off in chip stocks is picking up, and Nvidia shares are declining.
As the fallout from the downfall of the co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang goes on, lawmakers from
both parties say they want to know when Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick knew Huang was in
contact with a suspected Chinese asset, and whether the U.S. should tighten export controls
on advanced chips.
NPR's John Ruich reports.
There's an internal investigation into Huang's affair with the Chinese woman that will play
out at Nvidia.
Congress is also preparing to probe the spy allegations, which could put the company under
a hot spotlight.
Then there are all the relationships with Nvidia's partners and the deals that Huang handled
that are going to have to be tended to.
That includes some of the so-called circular financing agreements where Nvidia invests money
in companies that then turn around and buy chips for data centers.
Nvidia's board has tapped the company's CFO Collette Kress to take over.
One day after a crippling worldwide Microsoft outage, the company says it has addressed
the underlying technical problem, and there is broad recovery, but given the scale, services
are being restored gradually.
Microsoft 365 apps have some 430 million users globally.
Governments, schools, companies, and more found themselves unable to access Outlook email.
In some cases, jails were unable to release people on bail, and pharmacies were delayed
in accessing prescriptions.
The European Council President says diplomats from the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland
will go to Ukraine for peace talks.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky wants more support
from European allies.
He met with U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Whitkoff yesterday in Dublin, after
they had met with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Zelensky expressed frustration over the U.S.-controlled Star Shield satellite connection being slowed
down again.
He said Star Shield is vital to intercepting Russia's new jet-powered drones.
Putin called on Europe to end its support for Ukraine.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pyrenees, Kiev.
Mexico's president says a migrant caravan that was headed north has been disbanded.
NPR's Adr Peralta has this report.
In a social media post, President Trump warned that "huge caravans of migrants were beginning
their illegal march through Mexico."
He said if Mexico didn't stop them, he would double the tariffs on the country.
But the reality is that migration toward the United States is at historic lows.
Mexican President Claudia Shambaugh said her government had disrupted nearly two dozen
migrant caravans since the beginning of Trump's term.
And this new one has already dispersed.
Right now, there is no migrant caravan headed north, she says.
Migration has been a point of contention for these two countries.
But despite constant threats from Trump, Mexico has dodged nearly all new tariffs.
Adr Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
This is NPR News.
A new federal government study shows kids in some states are not prepared for kindergarten.
NPR's Jenaki Mehta reports.
Kindergarten is the entryway to public school.
But not all kids enter with the skills they need to succeed, including social and emotional
development, language acquisition, and motor skills.
The Government Accountability Office, an independent watchdog, looked at data from Connecticut,
Florida, Kentucky, Maryland, and Ohio to see how prepared its youngest were for kindergarten.
They found that fewer than half of students in all those states were ready.
White, Asian, or students in lower poverty areas had better odds of being prepared.
And districts with more children who had been to preschool were also more likely to have
students that came in ready for kindergarten.
Jenaki Mehta, NPR News.
Mauricio Pochettino, who led the U.S. men's national soccer team to a round of 16 finish
in the 2026 World Cup, is leaving.
He will take over as coach of the famed Manchester United.
Pochettino is the highest profile manager the U.S. had ever hired.
Before leaving, he will lead the U.S. team for two more games.
She's gotten close, but despite being nominated for eight Oscars, Glenn Close has never won.
Known for decades of starring roles including in Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, and more,
now the 79-year-old actor is receiving an honorary Oscar at the Governor's Awards.
She tells the Associated Press her first thought was she doesn't need a consolation prize,
but has since come to appreciate the honor.
You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: Nvidia shares fall as CEO Jensen Huang's downfall over suspected Chinese asset contact spreads
Congress and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick scrutinized over when Lutnick knew of Huang's contacts
Nvidia names CFO Colette Kress to take over after Huang's ouster and internal investigation
Microsoft says it fixed worldwide 365 outage affecting Outlook, courts, pharmacies, and governments
European diplomats from UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland to travel to Ukraine for peace talks
Zelensky meets U.S. envoys Kushner and Witkoff in Dublin, complains about slowed Starshield satellite service
Mexico's president says a migrant caravan headed north has been disbanded
Trump threatens Mexico with doubled tariffs over migrant caravans, which Mexico says it has blocked
Federal GAO study finds fewer than half of kindergarteners ready in five states including Ohio and Florida
Mauricio Pochettino leaving U.S. men's soccer team to coach Manchester United
Glenn Close to receive honorary Oscar at Governors Awards after eight nominations without a win
